question: Question linked to image nº35 A 25-year-old woman, with no relevant medical history, presenting a painless cervical adenopathy of 3 cm in diameter, slow-growing and two months old. The patient reports fever and night sweats. A biopsy of the adenopathy is performed. What is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Painless cervical adenopathy -> slow-growing -> fever and night sweats -> lymphoma -> 80% CHAIN: Biopsy of the adenopathy -> histopathological examination -> Reed-Sternberg cells -> lymphoma -> 85% CHAIN: Cervical adenopathy -> 3 cm in diameter -> two months old -> fever and night sweats -> lymphoma -> 80%
analysis: Given the clinical presentation of a painless cervical adenopathy with associated systemic symptoms like fever and night sweats, along with the slow growth of the adenopathy, the most likely diagnosis would be a lymphoma. Lymphomas often present with painless lymphadenopathy, systemic symptoms, and gradual enlargement of the lymph nodes.
